name: Nashira
description: A star 48 parsecs away, 4.9 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 106985: radius 4.893 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 56.761 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.062) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 106985: effective temperature 7167 +/- 206 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.051)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 3 from 2024A&A...681A.107R; the 7 published values span log g 2.56 to 4, across which the limb law changes by at most 2.7% of the centre brightness

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 106985: distance 48.146 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.035), at which the luminosity and radius hold

text.card: A star 48 parsecs away, 4.9 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 57 times the Sun's luminosity at 7,167 K, so 4.893 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 106985: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Gamma Capricorni
quotes.card: Gamma Capricorni is a star in the constellation of Capricornus.
quotes.introduction: Based on parallax measurements, it is located at a distance of approximately 171 light-years (52 pc) from the Sun.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 6838023243053666688 (quality A), from 2006AstL...32..759G; Gaia DR3 measures none
